paper.title: Differentially Private Language Generation and Identification in the Limit
paper.summary: Studies private generation and identification with the entire released trajectory visible under replacement of one input.

formalization_scope.summary: Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.5 and 1.6 have full proofs. Both parts of 1.3 hold for every k ≥ 2. Algorithm 2 and Theorem C.5 are proved.
specializations: Natural numbers encode words and hypothesis indices.
gaps: The singleton quantifier in 1.3 fails. For unrestricted positive privacy budgets the sharper coefficient in Appendix C.3 fails in both the one-shot and continual-release models.
The mathematical existence proofs of 1.1 and 1.6 use alternative algorithms.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the four unrestricted headline results, the corrected order lower bound, the C.3 counterexamples, and Algorithm 2 in Theorem C.5.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Five numbered main theorems of Section 1.1, with separate entries for the sharper lower bound C.3 and the online identification upper bound C.5 highlighted in the introduction.
exclusions: Other appendix items and remarks are not separately inventoried.
claim_inventory.notes: The PaperMap distinguishes the hard-family proof from the statement of Theorem 1.3.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: Public main results and the two counterexamples to the sharper Appendix C.3 coefficient.
exclusions: Auxiliary group-privacy and diagonal arguments and counterexamples to intermediate claims.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: The diagnostics are linked separately in the PaperMap.

claims.title: Private generation from a countable language collection
claims.statement_summary: Pure differential privacy of the full output stream is compatible with almost-sure generation for every target in a countable collection.

source_assessment.notes: An alternative construction uses the maximum finite intersection size of each public finite prefix of the family. The theorem establishes mathematical existence. The Laplace mechanism of Algorithm 1 and its oracle implementation have not been verified.

formalization.notes: An alternative construction uses the maximum finite intersection size of each public finite prefix of the family. The theorem establishes mathematical existence. The Laplace mechanism of Algorithm 1 and its oracle implementation have not been verified.

lean_links.notes: The construction works for every indexed family at each positive privacy budget, with probability-one eventual correctness for every injective enumeration.

audit_refs.scope: Checks Theorem 1.1 and its axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Private uniform generation sample upper bound
claims.statement_summary: For k languages of closure dimension d the high-probability continual-release threshold is at most d plus a polylogarithmic multiple of k times log(1/β) divided by ε.

source_assessment.notes: Finite subcollection selection is followed by uniform word release. A doubling schedule with telescoping budgets proves the continual bound for signed closure dimensions down to −1.

formalization.notes: Finite subcollection selection is followed by uniform word release. A doubling schedule with telescoping budgets proves the continual bound for signed closure dimensions down to −1.

lean_links.notes: For excess u of at least 33, the probability of any later failure is at most 10 exp(−εu/(8k(floor(log₂ u)+2)²)).

audit_refs.scope: Checks Theorem 1.2 and its axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Private uniform generation sample lower bound
claims.statement_summary: The paper claims hard collections with a uniform private generation threshold at least d plus order k/ε, while d+1 observations suffice without privacy.

source_assessment.notes: Definition 2 gives dimension −1 to a singleton infinite language. After (6) the proof infers success on an intersection from separate success probabilities. LowerBoundChecks gives a counterexample to this inference. MaskedRelease gives a private single-observation generator for every zero-dimensional family of size 4h with budget 3h log 2 + log 128. This refutes the stronger one-shot coefficient following C.3 when the privacy budget may grow with h. A continual generator pays one additional unit of privacy and satisfies both uniform success from the first observation and almost-sure eventual success. A separate packing argument proves the headline order lower bound for every k ≥ 2.

formalization.notes: Both bounds in the headline hold for every k ≥ 2 and every natural d. The singleton counterexample prevents the unrestricted statement.

components.summary: For every k ≥ 2 and d ≥ 0 there is a hard collection of size k and exact dimension d with the private order lower bound.
The unrestricted statement also asks for arbitrary natural dimensions at k = 1.

lean_links.notes: The order lower bound uses a marginal packing inequality on bit vectors. The hard collection has exactly k languages and closure dimension d for every k ≥ 2.
Applies to any collection satisfying the upper bound of Definition 2, using the P02 closure generator.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the repaired size range and both sample bounds.

claims.title: Private online identification barrier
claims.statement_summary: Distinct languages with infinite intersection and a finite one-sided difference rule out pure-private continual-release identification under adversarial presentations.

formalization.notes: Pure group privacy applies to joint output streams. A causal diagonal constructs an injective complete adversarial text.

lean_links.notes: The countable word universe is encoded by natural numbers. A correct run stabilizes at a single correct index.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public statement of Theorem 1.5 and its axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Stochastic private identification characterization
claims.statement_summary: Under independent draws with support equal to the target, private identification in the limit is possible exactly for collections satisfying Angluin’s finite tell-tale condition.

source_assessment.notes: An alternative sample-and-aggregate construction proves the existential sufficiency statement.

formalization.notes: Both directions hold at every positive privacy budget for the joint continual-release law. Sufficiency uses private aggregation on disjoint blocks.

lean_links.notes: A classical sample-and-aggregate learner stabilizes at the least correct index.

audit_refs.scope: Checks both directions of the stochastic identification characterization.

claims.title: Sharp leading term claimed for uniform private generation
claims.statement_summary: The source asserts a k log 2 − O(log k) lower bound on εm for a k-language family admitting guaranteed nonprivate generation from its first observation. It also asserts this bound for the one-shot problem on its explicit family.

source_assessment.notes: For k=4h, the public random choice to omit one of four blocks yields a one-shot mechanism using 3h log 2 + log 128 privacy. One additional unit suffices for the entire output stream, with almost-sure eventual correctness. These budgets beat any uniform logarithmic allowance for all sufficiently large h. The construction uses ε growing with k.

formalization.notes: The counterexamples are formalized for arbitrary logarithmic allowances. The order bound in the corrected headline theorem survives.

lean_links.notes: For every zero-dimensional family of the prescribed size, one private observation gives error at most one third.

Every family generatable nonprivately from the first observation admits a causal private generator satisfying the uniform two-thirds guarantee from that observation and almost-sure eventual correctness.

relations.notes: The sharper coefficient is separate from the order bound in the headline theorem.

claims.title: Private online identification under finite pairwise intersections
claims.statement_summary: The data-independent epoch exponential mechanism in Algorithm 2 is private under continual release and identifies the target online when the countably infinite family has finite pairwise intersections.

source_assessment.notes: Sections 1.1 and 2.1 highlight this positive counterpart to Theorem 1.5.

formalization.notes: The actual dyadic release schedule, overlap-based cap, negative inconsistency scores, and inverse-square privacy split of Algorithm 2 give pure privacy for the whole trajectory and almost-sure online identification under finite pairwise intersections.

lean_links.notes: Theorem C.5 applies to the explicit Algorithm 2 identifier. Indices start at zero. The privacy conjunct covers arbitrary streams. Correctness applies to injective enumerations.

audit_refs.scope: Checks Algorithm 2 privacy and almost-sure identification together.
